fieldNotes.location: Folgers/J.M. Smucker Old Gentilly Rd coffee roasting plant, New Orleans East. Confirmed via Street View (Nov 2025) showing the large industrial roasting building with processing tower and continuous perimeter fence/hedge, plus web research (largest bulk coffee facility of its kind in the world; opened 1960).
fieldNotes.truckGate: Wide gated truck entrance on the SW frontage road (~30.0316,-89.9135): a fence opening with sliding/swing gate panels set back from the road and an overhead gantry sign structure spanning the driveway. Clear controlled checkpoint.
fieldNotes.guardShack: No distinct staffed guard booth resolved at the gate in Street View or satellite; a small structure sits near the gate apron but its function is ambiguous. Low confidence — treated as remote check-in (kiosk/call-box).
fieldNotes.remoteGs: Set true because a controlled truck gate is present but no clear guard shack — implies kiosk / call-box check-in. Flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.shipRcvSeparate: Dock activity is split across more than one building face (south face dock apron near 30.0328,-89.9116 and a separate SE dock band near 30.0331,-89.9109); green coffee receiving and finished-goods shipping are physically distinct per site operations.
fieldNotes.railServed: Rail spur runs along the north edge of the property; web research confirms finished coffee ships by rail, truck and water.
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: Large multi-building campus: main roasting/packaging building, separate processing/silo structures to the NE, and ancillary buildings — more than one large cluster behind the fence.
fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: Gate driveway is wide with substantial unused paved apron width; room exists to add a bypass/express lane.
fieldNotes.dockDoorCount: ~30 estimate from overhead imagery; many bays partially obscured by building shadow and tree cover along faces. Flagged low confidence.
fieldNotes.siteAreaAcres: 73.8 acres for the full fenced manufacturing complex (building cluster plus rail-served processing yard and dock aprons). Historical 1960 footprint was ~20 acres; the operation has expanded substantially.
